newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Next Brazil coffee sale to be only 200,000 bags.
newsitem.headline: Next Brazil coffee sale to be only 200,000 bags.

text.p: Brazil's next auction from government coffee stocks will be for around 200,000 60-kg bags and will not contain any coffees exclusively for the soluble coffee industry, said a top government official.

"There will be no coffee just for the soluble industry as all the lower quality coffee is finished," said Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department at the Industry and Commerce Ministry.
The auction, to be held in May 7, is considerably smaller than the 326,188 bags contained in the last sale on April 2.
On that occasion, all 25,915 bags open only to the soluble industry was taken up, but only 102,745 of the 300,273 bags open to exports, roasters and the soluble industry were sold.
The soluble industry for some time has been complaining that higher internal Brazilian prices has damaged the industry's competitiveness in the international market.

Since February, the government has included lower quality coffees in its monthly auctions just for the soluble industry which producers in particular viewed as a preferable option to allowing the industry to import raw material.

Earlier this month, a producer official said growers wanted an end to split auctions. Traders said this was because growers now viewed imports more favorably when faced with the propspect of normal coffee being sold separately or at special prices.

The response from the soluble industry has been swift, with top soluble producer Companhia Cacique de Cafe Soluvel recently announcing that it is importing 20,000 bags of roasted coffee from India to be re-exported as soluble coffee.
